record.title: Liberia COVID land-border closure
record.scope: National passenger restrictions with phased onset and cargo/humanitarian exceptions
record.movement: Ordinary passengers and foreign commercial drivers; goods continued under restricted transfer arrangements.
record.exceptions: Humanitarian trucks and drivers under health controls; commercial and essential goods could be transferred at the frontier or carried onward by local drivers.
record.enforcement: Liberia Customs describes driver isolation, health checks, border unloading and driver substitution; post-by-post compliance is not independently established.
record.consequences: FrontPageAfrica reports disrupted supplies and concerns among traders in Ganta; wider losses are not quantified.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.context: FrontPageAfrica explicitly dates the Guinea/Côte d’Ivoire phase to 30 March 2020. The later Library of Congress summary reports the Sierra Leone phase on 1 April; its original basis is unverified.
record.uncertainty: 30 March is the explicit contemporary first-phase date. LOC’s 31 March dates that same article’s publication. The Sierra Leone phase and uniform onset remain incompletely verified. Customs provides a dated policy-status account, not a reopening or proof of uninterrupted enforcement.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. First phase reported 30 March; passenger restrictions documented by Customs on 4 May. Reopening unknown; no interval to cutoff inferred.
